title: Per-window delivery metrics, span handoff protocol, and redact-first logging for progressive outputs
creator: Anika Rao
description:
Goal: instrument progressive (streaming) API responses with a per-window metric model, a small span-handoff protocol for accurate trace continuity across partial outputs, and a redact-first logging approach that ensures PII/secret tokens are never persisted in raw logs.

Background: Current stream telemetry aggregates only per-request totals which hides tail behavior in progressive outputs. We need fine-grained visibility (per-window) to: detect micro-latency regressions, attribute cost to partial tokens, and correlate tool calls and function invocations that occur mid-stream. Simultaneously, traces must preserve parent-child relationships across multiple partial response commits to downstream consumers and proxies. Finally, logs emitted during streaming often contain sensitive fragments produced by models; we will apply redact-first transforms before any persistence.

Scope:
- Define a minimal "window" abstraction for the runtime (default 50ms or 32 tokens, configurable per model/profile).
- Emit metrics for each window: window_id, sequence_range, window_latency_ms, tokens_emitted, kv_cache_lookups, batch_size, retry_count, tool_calls_count, model_variant.
- Implement lightweight span-handoff: window spans are children of request-root; at the end of each window we emit an EndSpan with a handoff token in trace metadata so downstream continuations (e.g., tool call proxies, client-side reassembly) can stitch context.
- Redact-first logging: introduce layered scrubbers that run in the runtime hot-path before any log sink; default ruleset uses regex patterns for common PII and runtime token patterns plus a user-provided redact list. We will persist hashed fingerprints for debugging (one-way) to enable correlation without exposing raw content.

Non-goals: full content-aware NER redaction for arbitrary languages (this is a follow-up), client-side SDK changes for backcompat (handled in separate ticket).

Acceptance criteria:
1) Per-window metrics appear in infra metrics backend (Prometheus/OpenTelemetry) with appropriate tags and do not increase cardinality beyond a practical threshold.
2) Traces show continuous parent->child relationships across window boundaries for at least 95% of streamed requests in the canary test.
3) No raw streaming payloads containing PII are written to persistent logs in the canary; any sensitive fragments are replaced by stable fingerprints.
4) Backwards compatibility: clients that do not surface window IDs still receive coherent streaming responses; new metrics and spans are optional and gated behind a feature flag.

Implementation notes:
- Windowing will be implemented in the serving runtime core where token emission loop operates. We add a light weight Window object (immutable metadata, id).
- Metrics emission will batch to the metrics emitter every 200ms to avoid per-window network overhead. Metrics cardinality controls: model_variant and route are allowed labels; avoid including free-form strings.
- Span handoff uses a SHA256-based short token (first 12 chars) included as trace attribute "window_handoff"; the token is persisted only in tracing backends and hashed in logs.
- Redaction pipeline should run synchronously in the hot path but be optimized: precompiled regexes, a minimal whitelist-then-redact approach, and throttled hashing to avoid cost blowups.

Open design decisions:
- Default window size: 32 tokens vs 50ms latency. (tradeoff: resolution vs metric volume)
- Whether to emit a metric per-window or per-bounded-group of windows for very high throughput customers.

Migration/canary plan:
1) Merge runtime changes behind feature flag 'stream_window_metrics'.
2) Canary 1% of hosted traffic for low-traffic routes for 48 hours; monitor Prometheus and tracing for cardinality and latency impact.
3) Expand to 10% then control plane canary if OK.
4) Rollout to Dedicated with config flag available to ops teams.

Docs & artifacts:
- Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/Infra/Per-Window+Streaming+Telemetry (draft)
- Prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving/pull/7192 (WIP)
- Metrics dashboard (canary): https://dashboards.redwood.ai/d/streaming-window-health

Estimated work: 5 points across serving runtime (3), tracing integration (1), and logging/redaction (1).

2025-03-10 - Sofia Patel (security review): Requested that all fingerprints be one-way hashed with customer-specific salt and that we surface an opt-out for specific tenants. Added to design notes.
2025-03-11 - Marco Chen: Updated PR with hashed fingerprints and per-tenant opt-out config. Early canary harness setup in k8s namespace 'canary-window'.
2025-03-12 - Performance (internal): Saw 0.8% p50 latency increase for 1% canary on a 2-token bursty workload. Request to experiment with batching metrics every 200ms (implemented) and re-run.
2025-03-13 - Product (Liam Thompson): Approved canary plan; asked for an acceptance metric for tool_call attribution accuracy (~95% target). Added to acceptance criteria.
notes: Risk: metric cardinality explosion and hot-path CPU cost from redaction. Mitigations: label whitelist, batched emission, precompiled scrubbers, and per-tenant opt-out or sampling. Debugging knobs will be surfaced in telemetry: stream_window_sampling_rate and redact_hash_only mode.
next_steps: 1) Finish PR coverage and integration tests. 2) Run canary in low-traffic region and validate tracing continuity and absence of raw PII in logs. 3) Iterate on window sizing and metric batching based on canary data.
